psd.note: Full 4 s (2000-sample) epoch: 0.25 Hz bin spacing; 1 Hz full bandwidth -> NW = 2, 3 tapers.

band_rule: Half-open bins lo <= f < hi; band power = sum of PSD over the band's bins x bin width.
pairs_note: The 11 analysed homologous pairs (22 channels; Fp1/Fp2 and midline excluded), left channel first.

features.AI: (L - R) / (L + R) of band power, per epoch
features.LR: ln(L) - ln(R) of band power, per epoch
features.absAI: |AI| per epoch (then averaged), consistent with pdBSI
features.mabsAI: per epoch, mean of absAI over the available pairs, per band
features.pdBSI: per epoch, mean over available pairs and over PSD bins 1 <= f < 25 Hz of |(R - L) / (R + L)| (van Putten 2007)
features.DAR: per epoch, delta / alpha power summed over the available analysed channels
features.DTABR: per epoch, (delta + theta) / (alpha + beta) power summed over the available analysed channels

aggregation: Every feature is computed per epoch, averaged within each class (left_hand, right_hand), and the subject value is the mean of the two class means (class-balanced averaging, deviation D6).
missing_rule: A pair is NaN (no imputation) when either channel is in the epochs' info['bads'] (unavailable pair) or when both of its channels were interpolated at any stage (continuous-stage 'interpolated' or rule-iii 'screen_interpolated' in epoch_qc). Cross-pair features (mabsAI, pdBSI, DAR, DTABR) use the remaining pairs; the number used is recorded in the QC file.

lesion.rule: Approved lesion-alignment step (the only code that reads lesion side). For included subjects with a certain side: ipsilesional minus contralesional, i.e. les_AI = AI and les_LR = LR for a left lesion, and both sign-flipped for a right lesion; les_meanAI = mean of les_AI over available pairs. |AI| is sign-free and is not repeated. Subjects with an uncertain side have no row in the lesion table.

epoch_count_check: Label-free: Spearman rho of every feature with n_epochs_kept and with the smaller class count, across included subjects; reported, not used for any choice.
